A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Beryllium (베릴륨) itself — the sovereign of the Beryllium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: about twenty — a fresh young-adult face; no facial lines.
Face — her own: an elegant, refined presence; porcelain-pale skin; diamond-shaped face; medium-sized eyes — narrow upturned eyes, level outer eye corners; thin arched brows; small button nose; small bow lips; emerald-green eyes; a small beauty mark beside the lips.
Body and hair: slender build; a short tousled pixie cut with choppy uneven bangs; pale aquamarine hair with clear crystal-faceted highlights.
Expression: a faint soft smile, relaxed eyes.
Her element, carried in her design: beryllium: a light, very stiff steel-grey metal hidden inside beryl, the mineral that grows clear as green emerald and sea-blue aquamarine; found in 1798 by Vauquelin and first called glucinium because its salts taste sweet, though its dust is poisonous to breathe; freed as metal in 1828 by Wohler and Bussy using potassium; X-rays pass through it almost untouched; gold-coated hexagonal beryllium mirrors gather the first starlight in a great space telescope.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — MECHA
Costume: she is a female mecha personification — plates, joints, binders and glow lines carry the traits above; the plates must read as solid armor with visible joints, not as cloth or a gown; a back unit may carry the motif. Light, stiff steel-grey armor with a pair of large wing binders made of gold-coated hexagonal mirror segments spread symmetrically behind her like an unfolding space telescope, faceted aquamarine and emerald accents at the collar and hips, thin translucent window panels on the forearms; the plates must read as solid armor, not a gown.
Silhouette: large wing-shaped binder plates spread symmetrically behind her back as the main shape, with light body armor. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette.
Colours: pale aquamarine sea blue, deep emerald green, light steel grey, mirror gold.
Exposure (bold): her mecha frame is cut open by design in only these places — bare shoulders and upper arms between pauldron and gauntlet, and a deep open chest window with natural cleavage framed by the chest plates; everywhere else she stays fully plated. The plates stay on, fitted and symmetrical, with skin clearly showing in each opening. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; keep the plate material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: year 2200, a deep-space observatory: a vast telescope unfolding wings of gold-coated hexagonal mirrors above a tiered silver sunshield, white observation galleries lined with thin beryllium X-ray windows, the faint first starlight of the early universe gathered out of the dark.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: the scene's own light, rendered the way this style renders light and skin.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Be) and atomic number (4) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish.
